children: Favorable comments from US FDA scientists ahead of a Sept. 23 agency advisory committee meeting for GRAIL's
Galleri multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood test have propelled the company's shares ~34% higher in Monday trading.

"For many cancers, it is posited that earlier detection of cancer has the potential to improve patient outcomes by allowing for treatment initiation at a stage when curative treatment is more likely to be possible," the briefing document states. "A blood-based multi-cancer detection test may offer a valuable addition to existing screening approaches, particularly for cancer types for which few or no guideline-recommended screening options currently exist."

The document also provides members of the the Molecular and Clinical Genetics Panel of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee with a review of GRAIL's studies of Galleri for various types of cancer, including colon, lung, breast, prostate, head and neck, bladder, and kidney.

Results from GRAIL's PATHFINDER 2 study found that Galleri had a false positive rate of 0.15% and 0.26% in NHS-Galleri. The specificity rate — a measure of how accurate a negative result is — was 99.85% and 99.74% for, respectively, the two studies.

The panel will vote on three questions, summarized here: 1) Is Galleri safe to use in patients who meet criteria; 2) Is Galleri effective for patients who meet criteria?; and 3) Do the benefits of Galleri outweigh the risks?
